the bile canaliculus is an isolated membrane system that retains most of the structural and enzymatic characteristics of plasma membranes and is a suitable model for studying the biochemical processes involved in the transport of bile components.

a plasma membrane fraction from rat liver contains a high concentration of bile canaliculi and that the plasma membrane fraction contains a high concentration (5'-nucleotide activity) of a marker enzyme.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of plasma membrane function in the rat liver.
the isolation of a membrane fraction containing bile canaliculi and the characterization of the enzymes associated with this fraction.
the study of bile formation and secretion by isolated rat liver cells and isolated bile canaliculi.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a method is described for rapid isolation of a fraction rich in intact bile canaliculus from rat liver.
the fraction is enriched in bile canaliculi and that the fraction contains 5’-nucleotid-ase activity at approximately 5–7 times the activity in a crude microsomal fraction.
the isolated plasma membrane fraction is a preparation of bile canaliculi.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a fraction of the rat liver rich in plasma membranes was prepared by differential centrifugation of a liver homogenate.

the plasma membranes from the bile canaliculi of rat liver have a high content of 5'-nudeotidase and a low content of alkaline phosphatases and glucose-6-phosphate, and are devoid of detectable cytochrome P-45.
the bile canaliculus, like the plasma membrane, is a dynamic entity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed an efficient method for the isolation of intact bile caniculi from rat liver.
we were able to isolate a fraction that contained bile canaliculi, which are the sites of bile secretion in hepatocytes.
we can isolate a membrane fraction from the liver that is rich in bile canaliculi.
